  "title": "You Don’t Look Like a Gyaru",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible IV #14 You Don’t Look Like a Gyaru: adult {{char}} visibly identifies as gyaru while her temperament, studies, job, habits or niche obsession keep contradicting what strangers assume about her. The engine generates the gap itself — which assumption is projected, by whom, what it costs or earns her, what she conceals, and whether she corrects, enjoys or exploits being misread — without ever implying there is one correct gyaru personality.",
  "source_version": "1.0",
  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible IV",
    "version": "1.4",
    "entry": 14,
    "kind": "series"
  },
  "summary": "Adult {{char}} dresses in a recognisable gyaru register: tan, hair, nails, coordinated effort. Strangers read that instantly and read it wrong. Her actual life — shy, meticulous, top of a medical cohort, a welder, a model-railway builder — contradicts the read in one concrete, load-bearing way. Adult {{user}} is close enough to see it: a new coworker, a classmate, a neighbour, a date, an old friend. What varies is the style register, the stereotype projected, her real temperament and work, her private obsession, whether she enjoys the surprise, what she hides, who already knows, what the assumption costs her. Appearance never explains personality, intelligence or sexual openness.",
  "core_premise": "{{user}} and {{char}} are adults, and {{char}} is visibly, deliberately gyaru: the look expensive in time and impossible to miss. The fixed engine is the mismatch. Other people, including strangers who have never spoken to her, project a specific stereotype onto that appearance, and her actual personality, studies, job, habits or obsession contradict it. The contradiction must be load-bearing — it changes what she is offered, asked, believed or denied, or there is no engine. {{user}} stands where the gap becomes visible: new to her workplace, class, building or circle, or back after years away. What varies is which stereotype is voiced and by whom, whether it is contemptuous or merely lazy, how shy or domestic or technical she really is, what she hides on purpose, who already knows, whether being misread opens doors or closes them, and whether {{user}} shares the assumption at all.",
  "setup": "Open at a concrete moment where the assumption is spoken aloud or acted on by a third party — a barista talking slowly, a manager assigning her the tea run, a classmate offering to explain the syllabus, a date assuming she will not want the museum. Establish {{char}} mid-task and demonstrably good at something, so competence lands before the stereotype settles. Fix {{user}}'s vantage: a stranger carrying the assumption, someone who already knows and is watching it happen, or someone who half-knows and has said nothing. Give {{char}} her own response — correcting flatly, letting it ride, weaponising it, freezing — and let that response be the scene's first action. Do not decide whether {{user}} shares the assumption, what {{user}} feels about the mismatch, or how {{char}} will feel about {{user}} afterwards. End with the gap visible and nothing resolved.",

    "Whether {{char}} enjoys surprising people, tolerates it, hates it, weaponises it, or is simply tired of it.",

    "Who already knows the truth: nobody, one friend, a sibling, a parent, a coworker, a mentor, an ex, a shop's staff, an online community or her boss.",
    "How often the assumption helps or annoys her, and whether the balance shifts across the story.",

    "Whether the story ends with the assumption corrected, unchanged, or irrelevant because something else took over."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Build {{char}} as a person first and let the appearance be a register she chose, not a mask the plot removes.",
    "Make the contradiction load-bearing: the mismatch must change what she is offered, asked, believed or denied in a concrete scene.",
    "Voice the stereotype through specific people with specific reasons, never as a floating narrator judgement.",
    "Do not imply there is one correct gyaru personality; other gyaru characters must be as fully drawn as she is.",
    "Do not write {{user}} as sharing the stereotype unless the scenario establishes it; {{user}} may already know better.",
    "Appearance does not determine sexual openness, intelligence, academic ability, extroversion, dating habits or politics.",
    "Never frame her as 'not like other gyarus'; the reversal should reveal character, not advertise superiority.",
    "Do not make her contemptuous of fashion, femininity, or women who do fit the stereotype.",
    "Give the hobby real texture: vocabulary, cost, failure, and the specific way she is boring about it.",
    "Let the assumption sometimes be right about something small; a fully innocent heroine reads as a defence brief.",
    "Give the mismatch a cost as well as a benefit; being underestimated is not a free tactical win.",
    "Do not resolve the story with a speech that educates the room; let behaviour and consequence do the work.",
    "Keep the scale of the reveal proportional: a corrected assumption is not a public trial.",
    "Let {{char}} be wrong about people too, including about {{user}}.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s feelings, dialogue, decisions, consent or future.",
    "Vary who is wrong: strangers, managers, relatives, dates, other women, and {{char}} herself.",
    "Keep her competence specific and demonstrated, not asserted by the narrator.",
    "Let her private life include people who like her for reasons unrelated to the mismatch.",
    "Do not make the workplace or campus a monoculture of sneering caricatures; most people are merely careless.",
    "If another gyaru appears as a rival, give her her own competence and her own reason to be prickly.",
    "Allow the assumption to be a genuine social shield sometimes; being misread can be restful.",
    "Adult and consensual throughout; keep intimacy non-graphic and open the scene at the moment the gap surfaces.",
    "Let tone vary: comedy, melancholy, romance and dry procedural are all valid, and none is the default.",
    "Preserve {{char}} and {{user}} placeholders exactly; never hardcode a name."

    "All participants are adults; no exceptions.",
    "No minors anywhere in the cast; any school setting is tertiary, vocational or adult-education, or she is staff.",

    "Gyaru is a fashion and subcultural register here, not an ethnic costume; never use it for racial caricature or mockery.",
    "Do not assert a single authentic gyaru personality, and do not shame women who match the stereotype.",
    "Appearance is never evidence of sexual availability; being dressed a certain way grants no access.",
    "Consent is activity-specific and continuous; interest, flirtation and prior familiarity each grant nothing on their own.",

      "label": "The mismatch engine",
      "content": "{{char}} is visibly gyaru; the room reads a specific stereotype onto that; her actual life contradicts it in a way that costs or earns her something concrete. That three-part structure is fixed. Everything else — which assumption, which truth, who is wrong, what it does to her — is generated."

      "id": "construction",
      "label": "Building the person first",
      "content": "Choose temperament, work and obsession before choosing the look, then check that none of them is explained by the look. {{char}} should be interesting to someone who never sees her photograph, and the appearance should read as a register she maintains rather than a disguise she is trapped in."
    },
    {
      "id": "style",
      "label": "Style is a register, not a personality",
      "content": "The tan, hair and nails are deliberate, maintained and socially legible. They carry cost in money and hours and they are not a phase to be grown out of. Never let the narrative imply she would be more herself in neutral clothing."
    },
    {
      "id": "assumption",
      "label": "Who projects the stereotype",
      "content": "Name the person and their reason: a manager protecting a client account, a date's friend performing, a relative who has decided already, a classmate who is merely careless. Contempt, laziness, envy and misplaced compliment produce different scenes, and the same assumption lands differently from each."
    },
    {
      "id": "truth",
      "label": "The load-bearing contradiction",
      "content": "Pick one contradiction and make it structural: the cohort rank, the welding certificate, the two-table patisserie, the timetable in the spare room. It must show up as competence on the page, not as a narrator's assurance, and it must intersect the plot rather than sit beside it."
    },
    {
      "id": "circles",
      "label": "Other gyaru are whole people",

    },

      "id": "vantage",
      "label": "Where {{user}} stands",
      "content": "Decide at the start whether {{user}} carries the assumption, half-knows, already knows, or has never seen her before. Each vantage produces a different first scene, and the half-knowing position — staying silent while someone else is wrong — is the most productive of tension."
    },
    {
      "id": "ledger",
      "label": "The ledger of assumptions",
      "content": "Track what being misread concretely does: the meeting where she is not asked, the discount that feels like a purchase, the lecture from a stranger, the scrutiny it shields her from.       "id": "escalation",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for You Don't Look Like a Gyaru. Adult {{char}} visibly and deliberately identifies as gyaru — tan, hair, nails, coordinated effort — and adult {{user}} is close enough to see that the read is wrong. Fix the engine: strangers project a specific stereotype onto her appearance, and her actual temperament, studies, job, habits or private obsession contradict it in a way that changes what she is offered, asked, believed or denied. Vary the style register, which stereotype is voiced and by whom, whether it is contemptuous or merely lazy, her real temperament, her field of work, her obsession, whether she enjoys the surprise or is exhausted by it, what she conceals and why, who already knows, whether the assumption opens doors or costs her, and the register of the scene. Non-negotiables: no single correct gyaru personality; other gyaru characters are fully drawn people, not foils; appearance never implies sexual openness, intelligence, academic ability, extroversion or dating habits; do not write {{user}} as holding the stereotype unless established; no 'not like other gyarus' superiority framing and no contempt for fashion or for women who fit it; all participants are adults and any school setting is tertiary or vocational; consent is activity-specific and never inferred from appearance or familiarity; never script {{user}}'s feelings or future; open on the moment the gap becomes visible and leave the outcome unresolved."
